title: Local Regret Geometry of Empirical Welfare Maximization with Estimated versus Known Propensities
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; math review passed.
gap_reasons: The exact proportional-inflation frontier is proved only for a two-stratum, three-policy nested menu with independent coordinatewise added noise, so it does not establish a general ordering for EWM policy classes.

The pilot-and-grid construction attains the Gaussian-score value V, but V is explicitly not proved to be a minimax lower bound over all full-data procedures, so the note does not deliver a full local asymptotic minimax theorem.

The data-only minimax-transfer theorem states a substantive rate-and-attainment contribution but supplies no theorem-level comparison to the closest Gaussian plug-in/minimax or observed-data transfer result; add a precise comparator and state what its explicit selector, nonunique-LP construction, or O(n^{-1/12} log(n)^{1/3}) guarantee newly provides.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the canonical three-policy Gaussian regret identity, the proportional-inflation iff frontier, legal reversal witnesses, and a uniform observed-data transfer construction. A cited convex-set approximation was corrected from the i.i.d.-only Bentkus (2003) theorem to the source-matched independent-summand theorem of Raič (2019); D0.5 math review then passed. The independent novelty review graded the restricted package subfield, below the required field floor, and left a comparator-positioning request for the transfer theorem; no F-stage Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: For the bounded randomized two-stratum nested three-policy model, the exact canonical identity \(\Delta=P-(a+b)(vx-uy)K\) yields the proportional-inflation frontier and open near-tie regions with both strict regret rankings. Compact-uniform score and actual-risk approximations transfer that geometry to estimated- versus centered known-propensity EWM, including raw and globally demeaned scores and an all-positive-variance equal-\(2/3\)-propensity reversal. A fully data-measurable square-root-\(n\) pilot, certified Gaussian-program, and randomized-grid selector attains the Gaussian-score benchmark uniformly with \(B_n=O(n^{-1/12}\{\log(n+e)\}^{1/3})\). This benchmark is not asserted to be a lower bound over all full-data procedures.
gap: Kitagawa and Tetenov give known-propensity EWM rates and global demeaning, Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder give the propensity-score projection, and Hirano and Porter give the generic two-action Gaussian cutoff, essential-complete-class, and asymptotic minimax framework. None determines the sign of local expected actual regret for three nested policies. The scalar risk formulas used as a sanity check are derived directly in this proposal from the two-action local regret loss and are not attributed to Hirano--Porter Theorems 3.4--3.5. The Fang, Ridder, and Xie and Joo results are inspectable arXiv working papers that supply process-bound and Gaussian-decision machinery rather than this causal sign theorem.
fill: The canonical signed path identity and proportional-inflation dichotomy are mapped to row-specific estimated- and known-propensity EWM by a compact-uniform score approximation and two separate actual-risk approximations. Global centering and a bounded equal-propensity reversal connect the theorem to the JTPA scoring convention.
